no...darkness is absess of light. you can't turn nothing into something.

Think of 'light' as what it is - just electromagnetic energy. We can only perceive a very minuscule range of the entire electromagnetic spectrum for no reason other than that's how our eyes evolved. When we see darkness there is invariably plenty of electromagnetic energy out there, but we're just incapable of seeing it. When you go to the doctor and get an xray that 'invisible' energy it uses is no different than the visible light we perceived - it simply has a smaller wavelength than the light we can perceive. And similarly the reason we don't see a glow around warm objects like living bodies, similar to the way birds do, is because that energy has a larger wavelength than what we're capable of seeing. On a fundamental level we're almost entirely blind and only capable of perceiving, with the naked eye, a minuscule fraction of all EM energy out there.

That said I don't follow how exactly these crystals are supposed to work - it does not seem to be shifting infrared to visual as the person you're responding to suggested. But if something was capable of doing that, without power, it would indeed enable 'night vision' in plain old glasses.
